item.title: Deputy PM Rosso outlines vision for Customary Land Reform
item.description: Nearly 90 percent of land in Papua New Guinea remains under customary ownership today, a fact Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Lands, Physical Planning, and Urbanization, John Rosso, describes as a "unique national resource." Speaking at a High-Level Seminar on Customary Land, Rosso emphasized the Government’s responsibility to ensure land policies empower landowners to develop their property and benefit personally while contributing to the nation's growth. item.title: Customary land is heritage, not just an asset
item.description: In an address at the High-Level Seminar on Customary Land and Human Rights held at APEC Haus today, Coordinator of Project Sepik, Emmanuel Peni, issued a challenge to lawmakers drafting Papua New Guinea’s new land tenure bill. Peni argued that current legal frameworks often rooted in colonial and capitalistic perspectives fail to protect the 800 plus distinct cultural groups across the country.
